title: Malformed digest_ids can crash the sync route with a 500
reasoning: digest_ids is network-provided query input. The handler converts every comma-separated token with UUID(id_str) without validation or an HTTPException path. A malformed token raises ValueError inside the route, producing a server error instead of a client-facing 400/422 response. This also prevents the rest of sync from succeeding for otherwise valid clients with one bad cached ID value.
reproduction: Call the route with a non-UUID digest_ids value, for example GET /sync?digest_ids=not-a-uuid, with a valid API key. The UUID(id_str) conversion raises ValueError before the response is built.
recommendation: Parse digest_ids into UUIDs in a validated step. On invalid tokens, raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=...) or model the query parameter as a list/validated type so FastAPI returns a client error. Use the parsed UUID set in the NOT IN clause.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for this feature, and the owned file does not show route-level coverage for invalid digest_ids.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add a FastAPI route test that calls combined sync with digest_ids=not-a-uuid and asserts a 400 or 422 response rather than a 500.
minimumFixScope: app/api/sync.py digest_ids parsing and one route regression test
